factors.reason_template: Water is {value} C, inside preferred Pacific temperature range for pacific cod.
factors.value_notes: NOAA's 2022 Bering Sea trawl survey reports Pacific cod at bottom temperatures of approximately -1.6 to 8.4 °C in the eastern Bering Sea and -1.6 to 11 °C in the northern Bering Sea. These are bottom-trawl measurements, not satellite SST or a preferred-temperature curve. They cannot validate the configured 4-12 °C SST band or 6-10 °C ideal; keep values unchanged and mark needs_source.

factors.reason_template: Depth is {value} m, within prime Pacific depth zone for pacific cod.
factors.value_notes: NOAA describes Pacific cod as near-bottom fish on mud, sand and clay, moving from deep outer/upper shelf spawning grounds (about 300 to over 800 feet) in winter to shallower shelf feeding grounds in summer. A 2022 Bering Sea survey recorded bottom depths of 18-183 m in northern and eastern shelf areas; other NOAA species records span a much broader range. The configured 20-200 m interval is a reasonable shelf screen but not a universal depth preference across regions and seasons.
